holidays.name: National Milk Chocolate Day
holidays.description: A day to enjoy the smooth, creamy, sweet side of chocolate. Unwrap a bar, melt it into s'mores, or dunk strawberries in it. Dark chocolate gets plenty of attention, and today milk chocolate gets its turn.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food observance of unclear origin. It has become a fixture on July 28 in holiday calendars, and chocolate lovers keep it going.
holidays.funFact: Milk chocolate was invented in Switzerland in 1875. Daniel Peter created it by mixing cocoa with powdered milk, which Henri Nestlé had developed.

holidays.name: National Waterpark Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate wave pools, lazy rivers and towering slides. Grab your swimsuit and sunscreen, and plan on going down at least one slide screaming. Just don't forget your towel.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial summer observance of unclear origin. It falls at the height of summer, when water parks are at their busiest.
holidays.funFact: The first modern water park, Wet 'n Wild, opened in Orlando, Florida, in 1977. Water slides and wave pools have been a summer staple ever since.

holidays.name: World Nature Conservation Day
holidays.description: A global day to appreciate the natural world and take small steps to protect it. You could plant a tree, skip single-use plastics, or just go outside and say thanks to a forest.
holidays.origin: It is an annual awareness observance held on July 28. It encourages people to protect natural resources and keep ecosystems healthy for future generations.
holidays.funFact: Plants, animals and fungi depend on healthy ecosystems, and that includes the human species. Even small local actions like planting native flowers can help pollinators.
